title: How a private non-profit is fueling India’s sports medal tally
content:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed India’s desire to host the 2036 Olympics in Ahmedabad, with the country already submitting a letter of intent to the organizers.
• Olympic Gold Quest (OGQ)'s financial support grew from ₹19 crore in 2018-19 to ₹77 crore in 2024-25, with its budget now exceeding the ₹34.8 crore spent by the government's Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS).
• In 2024-25, Shitin Desai sold his 25% stake in Olympic Gold Quest (OGQ) to chess legend Viswanathan Anand, Sameer Koticha of ASK Group, and Niraj Bajaj of the Bajaj Group.

title: Iran to shift to ‘fully offensive’ posture as US peace talks stall: Report
content:
• A memorandum of understanding (MoU) was signed by the US and Iran in June (specifically June 17), giving them 60 days to negotiate a broader agreement, with a final peace agreement expected by the reported Monday.
• Before the war, approximately a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments passed through the strategic Strait of Hormuz.
• US President Donald Trump ruled out extending the interim ceasefire agreement and expressed a plan to declare the Strait of Hormuz "a territory of the United States" after the war, while Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei asserted Iran's existing sovereign rights over the waterway.

title: UK PM Andy Burnham exchanged messages with Susie Wiles impersonator before suspecting contact was fake: Report
content:
• UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham exchanged messages with an impersonator of Susie Wiles, US President Donald Trump’s chief of staff.
• Andy Burnham became the UK Prime Minister on July 20.
• The British embassy in Washington raised concerns with the White House regarding the impersonation incident.

title: US Navy destroyer hit by 4-day power failure in South China Sea amid Iran war strain: Report
content:
• The USS Benfold, an Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer, suffered an engineering failure involving its generators on July 24, leading to a 4-day power outage.
• After four days without power, the USS Benfold was towed to Subic Bay in the Philippines for repairs, which were completed on August 8.
• The USS Abraham Lincoln has spent more than 240 days without a port call while supporting US military operations against Iran.

title: Senior IAS officer Anurag Jain takes over as NITI Aayog CEO
content:
• Anurag Jain, a 1989-batch IAS officer of the Madhya Pradesh cadre, assumed charge as the new CEO of NITI Aayog on Monday, succeeding B.V.R. Subrahmanyam.
• Anurag Jain has been appointed as the NITI Aayog CEO for a two-year term, effective from the date he assumes charge.
• NITI Aayog was constituted on 1 January 2015, and its leadership was reconstituted in April this year, with Ashok Kumar Lahiri appointed as Vice-Chairman, replacing Suman K. Bery.

title: No signs of ‘foul play’ in Hayden Panettiere’s death, say Greenville Police
content:
• Actress Hayden Panettiere, 36, was found dead at an apartment complex in South Carolina on Sunday, August 16.
• The Greenville Police Department and Greenville County Coroner’s Office are investigating Panettiere's death, with preliminary findings indicating no signs of foul play.
• Hayden Panettiere, known for roles in 'Heroes' and 'Nashville,' earned three Teen Choice Awards and two Golden Globe nominations during her career.

title: ICRA estimates India's GDP growth at four-quarter low of 7 per cent in April-June
content:
• Rating agency ICRA estimated India's GDP growth at a four-quarter low of 7 per cent in the April-June quarter of 2026-27.
• ICRA projects India's real GDP growth to moderate to 6.7 per cent for the full 2026-27 fiscal, down from 7.7 per cent in 2025-26.
• India's nominal GDP expansion is projected by ICRA to accelerate to a four-year high of 13 per cent in 2026-27, compared to 8.9 per cent in 2025-26.

title: RBI cuts FX swap window short after NRI deposits cross $50 billion
content:
• The RBI cut its FX swap window short after Non-Resident Indian (NRI) deposits crossed $50 billion in approximately two months.
• Indian authorities' measures have brought in nearly $57 billion in overseas fundraising, helping shore up foreign exchange reserves to more than $700 billion.
• Economists at Citi trimmed India's Balance of Payments (BoP) surplus forecast to $53 billion from an earlier $60 billion for the year ending March, projecting a deficit in October-December.

title: IISR signs MoU with Bio Mountain Farmers Producer Company, launches AI-enabled web applications
content:
• Indian Institute of Spices Research (ICAR-IISR), Kozhikode, signed an MoU with Bio Mountain Farmers Producer Company Limited, Kannur, to strengthen collaboration in disseminating improved spice production technologies.
• ICAR-IISR entered into a licensing agreement with Botagnix Private Limited, Jalna, Maharashtra, for the commercial production and marketing of its novel granular formulation of Lecanicillium psalliotae for cardamom.
• Two new licenses were issued for the IISR black pepper variety IISR Chandra, facilitating its wider dissemination and commercial utilisation.
